rationale:
Split. The supplied proof of polyhedral_approx_finite_mass_seq rests on four general facts. None of them involves lattices, the deformation theorem or integrality, and each is a reusable Chapter-6 lemma or a real-analysis lemma.
(1) mass_estimate, from proof steps 1 and 3: |Y(η)| ≤ C·M(Y) when |η| ≤ C. This is exactly the comparator-accepted declaration br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass (node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.lattice_approximation-a1.mass_estimate-a1, status accepted, candidate d771ac3). It is reused with a byte-identical frozen type, which the controller's _existing_lean_name_problem rule allows for accepted nodes, so it needs no new work.
(2) testform_bounded, from proof step 2: every test form has a positive bound on its Euclidean coefficient norm. The identical statement is pending under another parent as br_la_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded, status comparing. An unaccepted node owned by another parent cannot be shared, so this child gets the fresh name polyhedral_approx_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded.
(3) scale_sequence, from proof step 4: every real sequence a_k admits positive antitone scales ρ_k → 0 with ρ_k·a_k ≤ 1/(k+1). This is pure real analysis and contains the only induction of the proof.
(4) flat_convergence, from proof step 6 and the printed 'Evidently (1), (2) give P_k(ω) → T(ω)': if X_k − Pc_k = ∂R_k + S_k with M(R_k) → 0 and M(S_k) → 0, then Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0. It is stated for sequences X_k and an arbitrary U, so it strictly generalizes the fixed-X lemma of the boundary-rectifiability branch. It depends on (1) and (2).

The parent proof is the supplied proof with steps 1–4 and 6 delegated to the children:
- Take C from DeformationTheorem for (m, ℓ, 1 ≤ ℓ). Put a_k := (M(X_k) + M(∂X_k)).toReal and obtain ρ from (3).
- For each k, apply DeformationTheorem to X_k at scale ρ_k > 0 and choose Pc_k, β′_k, R_k, S_k.
- Using IsIntegerMultiplicity X_k, choose β_k(F) ∈ ℤ with β′_k(F) = β_k(F). Rewriting β′_k = (F ↦ (β_k F : ℝ)) gives the lattice-chain conjunct.
- Since M(X_k) + M(∂X_k) = ofReal(a_k), we get M(R_k) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_k)·M(X_k) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_k·a_k) ≤ C·ofReal(1/(k+1)) → 0. The same bound holds for M(S_k), using M(∂X_k) ≤ ofReal(a_k).
- Then (4) with U = univ and n = m+1 gives Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0 for every ω. The three ρ conjuncts come from (3).

subproblems.title: Mass inequality |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y) under a pointwise bound |ω| ≤ C
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set, let Y ∈ D_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n, i.e. a smooth compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U). Let C ∈ ℝ with C > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm. Assume the mass M(Y) = Y.mass = M_U(Y) is finite. Then |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y), where M(Y) ∈ [0, ∞) is read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (C : ℝ), 0 < C → (∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → Y.mass ≠ ∞ → |Y ω| ≤ C * Y.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5: M(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with |ω| ≤ 1, using the Euclidean coefficient norm of Remark 2.6. This is steps 1 and 3 of the parent proof, written for an arbitrary set U and degree n. It is exactly the already comparator-accepted declaration Submission.br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass (DAG node root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.lattice_approximation-a1.mass_estimate-a1, candidate d771ac3), reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation.
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0)), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.
- By definition Y.mass = Y.massOn U is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η)) over η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U. That set consists of the η ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ U and |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
- In particular (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η)) ≤ Y.mass for every such η.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and an n-covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|.
   - (tα)(v) = t·α(v). So for strictly increasing I the summand ((tα)(e_I))² equals t²·α(e_I)², and for any other I both summands are 0 = t²·0.
   - Factoring t² out of the finite sum (Finset.mul_sum), the sum for tα is t²·s, where s ≥ 0 is the sum for α.
   - Hence |tα| = √(t²·s) = √(t²)·√s = |t|·√s = |t|·|α| (Real.sqrt_mul (sq_nonneg t), Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
   - The library also gives |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (Admissibility.) Let η ∈ Dⁿ(U) satisfy |η(x)| ≤ C for all x ∈ ℝ^P, and put η′ := C⁻¹·η.
   - Dⁿ(U) is a real submodule, so η′ ∈ Dⁿ(U). In particular tsupport η′ ⊆ U, the second component of the TestFormOn property.
   - η′(x) = C⁻¹·η(x). By step 1 and C⁻¹ > 0, |η′(x)| = C⁻¹·|η(x)| ≤ C⁻¹·C = 1 for every x.
   - Hence η′ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, and ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η′)) ≤ Y.mass.
3. (One-sided bound.) Since Y.mass ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal(r) ≤ Y.mass is equivalent to r ≤ Y.mass.toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal). Y is linear, so Y(η′) = C⁻¹·Y(η) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence C⁻¹·Y(η) ≤ Y.mass.toReal. Multiplying by C > 0 (inv_mul_le_iff₀) gives Y(η) ≤ C·Y.mass.toReal.
4. Apply steps 2–3 twice.
   - To η := ω, which satisfies |ω(x)| ≤ C by hypothesis: Y(ω) ≤ C·Y.mass.toReal.
   - To η := −ω, which satisfies |(−ω)(x)| = |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ C by step 1. Since Y(−ω) = −Y(ω) (map_neg for the linear functional Y.toCurrent), this gives −Y(ω) ≤ C·Y.mass.toReal.
5. Together, |Y(ω)| = max(Y(ω), −Y(ω)) ≤ C·Y.mass.toReal (abs_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| for the Euclidean coefficient norm (factor t² out of the sum of squares; √(t²s) = |t|√s).
If |η| ≤ C pointwise then C⁻¹η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, so ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·Y(η)) ≤ M(Y).
Because M(Y) ≠ ∞ this gives Y(η) ≤ C·M(Y).toReal.
Apply to η = ω and η = −ω to obtain |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y).toReal.

subproblems.title: Every test form has a finite Euclidean coefficient sup norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n: a smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞), compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then there is a real number C > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof: a test form is continuous with compact support, so the supremum of its Euclidean coefficient norm is finite (Simon Ch. 6, 1.15 and 2.4). Here this finiteness is proved directly for the real function x ↦ |ω(x)|, using continuity of |·| rather than the comparison |α| ≤ √N·‖α‖ with the operator norm. The conclusion is the same.

Notation. Λⁿ := Covector (Eucl P) n is the normed space of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ. For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0)).

1. (|·| is continuous on Λⁿ.)
   - For each fixed v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, the evaluation α ↦ α(v) is continuous on Λⁿ (continuous_eval_const, via the instance ContinuousAlternatingMap.instContinuousEvalConst).
   - Hence for each I : Fin n → Fin P, the summand α ↦ (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0) is continuous. It is either the square of a continuous function or the constant 0.
   - A finite sum of continuous functions is continuous (continuous_finsetSum), and the square root is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt). So α ↦ |α| is continuous.
2. (Continuity of f.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞, the first component of the test-form property of ω), hence continuous. Therefore f(x) := |ω(x)| is continuous on ℝ^P, as a composition of continuous maps.
3. (Compact support of f.)
   - If ω(x) = 0 then f(x) = |0| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Hence support f ⊆ support ω ⊆ tsupport ω.
   - ω has compact support (the second component of IsTestForm), so f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono').
4. (Boundedness.) A continuous, compactly supported real function is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C₀ ∈ ℝ with ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P. In particular C₀ ≥ ‖f(0)‖ ≥ 0.
5. Put C := C₀ + 1. Then C ≥ 1 > 0, and for every x ∈ ℝ^P, f(x) ≤ |f(x)| = ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C₀ < C. So |ω(x)| ≤ C for all x. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous on Λⁿ: continuous evaluations, a finite sum of squares, and the square root.
f(x) = |ω(x)| is continuous because ω is smooth.
f has compact support because |0| = 0 and ω has compact support.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C₀ ≥ 0; take C = C₀ + 1 > 0.

subproblems.title: Positive antitone null scales adapted to a given real sequence
subproblems.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℝ be an arbitrary real sequence. Then there is a sequence ρ : ℕ → ℝ such that ρ_k > 0 for every k ∈ ℕ, ρ is antitone (ρ_l ≤ ρ_k whenever k ≤ l), ρ_k → 0 as k → ∞, and ρ_k·a_k ≤ 1/(k+1) for every k ∈ ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, ∃ ρ : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < ρ k) ∧ Antitone ρ ∧ Tendsto ρ atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ k, ρ k * a k ≤ 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (Scales) of the parent proof, which chooses the scales ρ_k ↓ 0 of Simon 6.2 according to the masses. The parent applies this with a_k = (M(X_k) + M(∂X_k)).toReal ≥ 0. Here a_k is arbitrary, so 1 + a_k is replaced by b_k := 1 + |a_k|; this equals 1 + a_k when a_k ≥ 0, giving exactly the parent's construction.

1. Put b_k := 1 + |a_k|. Then b_k ≥ 1 > 0 for every k.
2. Define ρ recursively: ρ_0 := 1/b_0 and ρ_{j+1} := min{ρ_j, 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1})} for j ∈ ℕ. (In Lean, use Nat.rec; both defining equations then hold by rfl.)
3. (Positivity.) By induction on k.
   - ρ_0 = 1/b_0 > 0.
   - If ρ_j > 0, then ρ_{j+1} is the minimum of ρ_j > 0 and 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1}) > 0, hence positive (lt_min).
4. (Antitone.) ρ_{j+1} ≤ ρ_j for every j (min_le_left), so ρ is antitone (antitone_nat_of_succ_le).
5. (Upper bound.) For every k, ρ_k ≤ 1/((k+1)·b_k).
   - For k = 0: ρ_0 = 1/b_0 = 1/((0+1)·b_0).
   - For k = j+1: ρ_{j+1} ≤ 1/((j+2)·b_{j+1}) (min_le_right). Moreover (j+1)+1 = j+2; for the casts ℕ → ℝ, ((j+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 = (j : ℝ) + 2 (push_cast, ring).
6. (Limit.)
   - Since b_k ≥ 1, (k+1)·b_k ≥ k+1 > 0. So step 5 gives ρ_k ≤ 1/((k+1)·b_k) ≤ 1/(k+1) (one_div_le_one_div_of_le).
   - Thus 0 < ρ_k ≤ 1/(k+1) for all k, and 1/(k+1) → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). By the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero), ρ_k → 0.
7. (Product bound.) Fix k.
   - Since ρ_k > 0 and a_k ≤ |a_k|: ρ_k·a_k ≤ ρ_k·|a_k|.
   - By step 5 and |a_k| ≥ 0: ρ_k·|a_k| ≤ |a_k|/((k+1)·b_k).
   - Since 0 ≤ |a_k| ≤ 1 + |a_k| = b_k and (k+1)·b_k > 0: |a_k|/((k+1)·b_k) ≤ b_k/((k+1)·b_k) = 1/(k+1).
   - Hence ρ_k·a_k ≤ 1/(k+1).
Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 give the four required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: ρ_k > 0 by induction; ρ is antitone because ρ_{j+1} ≤ ρ_j.

subproblems.title: Flat decompositions with vanishing masses give pointwise convergence of the differences
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. For k ∈ ℕ let X_k, Pc_k, S_k ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R_k ∈ D_{n+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1)). Assume X_k(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = ∂R_k(ω) + S_k(ω) for every k ∈ ℕ and every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U). Assume also M(R_k) → 0 and M(S_k) → 0 in [0, ∞] as k → ∞, where M(·) = mass = M_U(·). Then Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0 as k → ∞ for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X Pc S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)), (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn U n), X k ω - Pc k ω = (R k).boundary ω + S k ω) → Tendsto (fun k => (R k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun k => (S k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Tendsto (fun k => Pc k ω - X k ω) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 6.2, printed proof (p. 169). It has (1) T − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k and (2) M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(T) → 0, M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂T) → 0, followed by 'Evidently (1), (2) give P_k(ω) → T(ω)'; the printed 'T_k(ω)' is a misprint for T(ω). This is step 6 of the parent proof, written for sequences X_k, Pc_k and an arbitrary set U. It uses two sibling lemmas:
- mass_estimate: |Y(η)| ≤ C·M(Y).toReal whenever C > 0, |η(x)| ≤ C for all x, and M(Y) ≠ ∞.
- testform_bounded: every test form η has some C > 0 with |η(x)| ≤ C for all x.

Notation: |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α and M(Y) = Y.mass.

1. Fix ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and put dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω ∈ D^{n+1}(U). By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω) for every k. So the hypothesis reads X_k(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = R_k(dω) + S_k(ω), i.e. Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) = −(R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)) for every k.
2. By testform_bounded, in degree n for ω and in degree n+1 for dω, choose C₀ > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P, and C₁ > 0 with |dω(x)| ≤ C₁ for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
3. (Finiteness and real limits.)
   - Since M(R_k) → 0 and 0 ≠ ∞, the set {t ∈ [0, ∞] : t ≠ ∞} is a neighbourhood of 0 (eventually_ne_nhds). So M(R_k) ≠ ∞ for all sufficiently large k. Likewise M(S_k) ≠ ∞ for all sufficiently large k.
   - ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), and (0 : [0, ∞]).toReal = 0. Hence M(R_k).toReal → 0 and M(S_k).toReal → 0 in ℝ.
4. (Estimate.) Let k be large enough that M(R_k) ≠ ∞ and M(S_k) ≠ ∞; by step 3 this holds for all sufficiently large k.
   - mass_estimate with Y = R_k, form dω and constant C₁ gives |R_k(dω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal.
   - mass_estimate with Y = S_k, form ω and constant C₀ gives |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₀·M(S_k).toReal.
   - With step 1 and the triangle inequality: |Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)| = |R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)| ≤ |R_k(dω)| + |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal.
5. (Squeeze.) By step 3, the right-hand side C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal tends to C₁·0 + C₀·0 = 0 (Tendsto.const_mul, Tendsto.add). The bound of step 4 holds for all sufficiently large k, so the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm', with ‖r‖ = |r| on ℝ) gives Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0. Since ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) was arbitrary, the claim follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: testform_bounded gives C₀, C₁ > 0 bounding |ω| and |dω| everywhere.
M(R_k) and M(S_k) are eventually finite, and their toReal values tend to 0.
mass_estimate gives |Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)| ≤ C₁·M(R_k).toReal + C₀·M(S_k).toReal eventually.
